1.explanation:
1. src/js/components/DateInput/README.md – explains the DateInput API and calendarProps, so you can see how bounds are configured.
2. src/js/components/DateInput/stories/typescript/DefaultValue.tsx – this story demonstrates defaultValue with a timezone offset, matching the bug’s setup.
3. src/js/components/DateInput/stories/typescript/CalendarBounds.tsx – shows how bounds are passed into the DateInput’s calendarProps, used to reproduce disabling logic.
4. src/js/components/Calendar/README.md – details the Calendar component’s bounds prop and how it should disable out-of-range days.
5. src/js/components/Calendar/stories/CustomThemed – has example usages of Calendar with custom bounds, useful to verify the Calendar behavior in isolation.
6. src/utils – contains date utility functions (parsing, comparisons, timezone adjustments) that underlie both DateInput and Calendar and may reveal where the offset logic is incorrect.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a Grommet DateInput with a defaultValue in July 2020 (with timezone offset) but its calendarProps bounds are set to ['2020-07-01', '2020-07-31']. Despite those bounds, the previous month’s day (June 30) remains enabled and selectable (highlighted in purple). In the calendar grid you can see “June 2020” at the top, the left-arrow navigation, and day cells “1–30” of June. Day 30 is not greyed out and can be clicked, even though it falls outside the defined bounds. The bug likely involves the DateInput’s bounds logic, how it passes those bounds to the underlying Calendar component, and how date comparisons behave when a defaultValue includes a timezone offset.
